doc.title: Contributing
doc.paragraph:
GitHub hosts the Adaptive Framework source code repository. We use the
GitFlow branching model to track the development and releases of the framework. The main branch is the default and most current version of the framework. The develop branch is used for the next release. A feature branch is sometimes used for major, long-term development features. For collaborators outside of the organization, we do accept Pull Requests using the "fork and pull" workflow.

section.title: Coding Conventions
section.paragraph: These conventions are not required, but are followed in AFW core unless noted in the associated header file:

list.item: Adaptive object property names should be lower camel case (i.e., first character lower case). For a limit or cap, use a max… id (for example maxNumberOfParameters, maxReadBytes, maxValue). Write “Maximum …” in briefs and labels, not in the property id.
The id of objects of type AdaptiveObjectType, AdaptivePropertyType, and AdaptiveDataType should be upper camel case (ie. first character upper case).
All names declared in headers should start with the header name without the .h. For instance all of the function names in afw_memory.h begin with afw_memory_.
All #define names in headers should start with the uppercased header name without the .h. For instance all of the #define names in afw_memory.h begin with AFW_MEMORY_.

All #define names should be uppercase with the exception of the parts of a name that matches the case of the thing they represent. For instance, the #define name for the core quoted string for "objectType" is AFW_Q_objectType.
Q in a #define name indicates a quoted preprocessing value.
U in a #define name indicates an unquoted preprocessing value.
S in a #define name indicates a reference to a string variable containing a s in it's name.
s is in the variable name of a afw_utf8_t that is referenced externally.
The variable name of null-terminated strings end with a _z.

A function name with _as_ and a data type id, such as afw_object_get_property_as_string(), returns the typed value (const afw_value_string_t *). It does not convert or evaluate. The same name ending in _internal, such as afw_object_get_property_as_string_internal(), returns the C value inside it (const afw_utf8_t *). A name with convert_to_, such as afw_value_convert_to_string(), converts.

A create function says where what it makes lives. create_unmanaged makes something that lives in the pool you pass and goes when that pool goes. create_unmanaged_new_p and create_unmanaged_cede_p make something with a pool of its own that is freed when its last reference is released. create_managed makes something that is kept by reference in the pool's managed_p; its caller releases it.

Property names are passed as values (const afw_value_t *), not as afw_utf8_t. Each name in a source directory's generate/strings/ gives you both: afw_v_objectType is the value to pass as a property name, and afw_s_objectType is the afw_utf8_t for everything else. Other source directories use their own prefix, such as afw_lmdb_v_.

Source file copyright banners stay Copyright (c) 2010-2024 Clemson University (or the range already on that file). Do not roll the end year forward to the current calendar year when adding or editing a file.

section.title: Versioning
section.paragraph: The version of a package is the version property in its afw-package.json. When you generate, afwdev writes it into a header in each source directory's generated/ directory. For core that is src/afw/generated/afw_version_info.h, with AFW_VERSION_MAJOR, AFW_VERSION_MINOR, AFW_VERSION_PATCH, AFW_VERSION_HEX and AFW_VERSION_STRING. Other source directories get the same set with their own prefix, for example AFW_LMDB_VERSION_STRING in afw_lmdb_version_info.h. To change the version, change afw-package.json and build with ./afwdev build --cdev or --fulldev. Do not edit the generated header.

Function afw_version_check(), in version/afw_version.c, decides whether code compiled against one version can run with this libafw. Before 1.0, the MAJOR and MINOR versions must be the same. From 1.0 on, MAJOR must be the same and the library's MINOR must be the same or larger. PATCH may differ either way. Update this function when the compatibility rules change.

Any Adaptive Framework application should pass AFW_VERSION_HEX as the first parameter to afw_environment_create(). Macro AFW_ENVIRONMENT_CREATE() will do this for you. Function afw_environment_create() will insure that the version of the Adaptive Framework library and its dependencies are compatible with the application.

Function afw_environment_load_extension() checks the version of libafw that the extension was compiled against to make sure it is compatible. An extension records that version with AFW_ENVIRONMENT_DEFINE_EXTENSION_IMPL(). Because the check before 1.0 only compares MAJOR and MINOR, it does not catch everything: rebuild your extensions and commands whenever you install a new Adaptive Framework.

section.title: Before You Open a Pull Request
section.paragraph: For most changes, building with ./afwdev build --cdev and running afwdev test -j as you go is enough. Before you open a pull request that changes C, or anything that is generated into C, we run the whole build and every test mode once:
section.code: ./afwdev build --fulldev afwdev test -j --baseline afwdev test -j --env-mode valgrind --baseline ./afwdev build --cdev --sanitize address afwdev test -j --env-mode asan --baseline
section.paragraph: The valgrind run takes a while, and the AddressSanitizer pair about seven minutes more. The two find different problems, so we run both. The AddressSanitizer build goes into its own tree, build/asan/cmake/, and never changes what is installed, so the order of the two pairs does not matter. --baseline saves each run as your branch's baseline for that mode, and later branches compare their memory use against it (see Writing Tests).

Valgrind and AddressSanitizer test the C runtime, so other changes need less. A change to afwdev (but not its generators) needs ./afwdev build --cdev and afwdev test -j --baseline. A change to the administrative web application needs ./afwdev build --js and afwdev test --js. A change to the handbook needs a clean ./afwdev build --docs -j.
